name: Defense
blurb: Decision support, autonomy, and ISR processing as programs of record; DIU as the commercial on-ramp; free federal procurement data first, subscription analysts labeled.

points.desc: The Defense Innovation Unit is where commercial AI enters DoD programs, with public project listings.
points.name: DIU is the commercial gateway

points.desc: Federal AI research organisations are tracked in the Government Labs section.
points.name: Government AI labs are catalogued here

points.desc: The government's own system of record for federal contract opportunities - AI-related DoD solicitations, awards, and vendor registrations, free and searchable.
points.name: SAM.gov is the primary record of solicitations

points.desc: Every federal award, downloadable - contract spending on AI-related solutions traces here, built on the Federal Procurement Data System feed.
points.name: USAspending carries the award data

points.desc: The Federal Procurement Data System records DoD contract actions and vendor performance history at the transaction level.
points.name: FPDS is the underlying procurement system

points.desc: The defense-intelligence platform used inside the Department tracks procurement trends, supply-chain risk, and vendor capability in AI and autonomy, publishing public scorecards on critical-technology spending.
points.name: Govini builds decision science on that record

points.desc: The nonprofit monitors the intersection of commercial tech, private capital, and national security, publicly mapping the companies driving AI adoption in the DoD space.
points.name: Silicon Valley Defense Group maps the commercial entrants

points.desc: Long-running defense analysis providers maintaining databases of contractors, programs, and procurement forecasts - subscription sources, named for completeness.
points.name: Janes and Forecast International cover the defense-industrial base

summary: Decision support, autonomy, and ISR processing are the programs of record; DIU is the commercial on-ramp. Who tracks the sector: free government procurement databases are the primary record, with dedicated defense-intelligence firms layered on top - this page starts with the sources anyone can verify.
